attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, framed as his updated hypothesis. Not a quotation of anyone else; the NYT quote that follows is separate supporting material.

semantics.note: 'I believe... will have to raise' is unqualified expectation of a definite outcome, so it is scored. Revision 2 keeps the necessity ('have to'), the antecedent (current round closing), the size threshold and the July 2025 horizon.

contract.note: Reading 'have to' as raised plus OpenAI's own stated need is fair, since true necessity is untestable. The $6.6B threshold and the 2025-07-31 end match his words. The outcome does not depend on a disputed reading: a $40B round with a $10B planned first closing clears any reasonable threshold.

evidence.note: OpenAI disclosure dated 2024-10-02 that the $6.6B round was raised. It establishes the antecedent and the size threshold; it is evidence of the condition, not of the outcome.
Company disclosure dated 2024-12-27, inside the horizon, stating it needs to raise more capital. It meets the contract's stated-need requirement but does not prove actual necessity.
Company disclosure dated 2025-03-31 announcing a $40B round. This is inside the horizon and far above $6.6B.

Investor disclosure of a definitive agreement signed 2025-03-31 for up to $40B, with a $10B first closing planned for mid-April 2025, inside the horizon. Completion of payment is not confirmed in the packet, but the contract only requires a planned closing.

output.rationale: The antecedent was met on 2024-10-02 ($6.6B raised). Before the 2025-07-31 deadline, OpenAI stated it needed more capital (Dec 2024). It then announced a $40B round on 2025-03-31, and SoftBank disclosed a signed agreement with a $10B first closing planned for April 2025. That meets every part of the support condition. Necessity rests only on company disclosures. No counterevidence was found.
